reviews.text: This is a place where you can enjoy steamed clams and grilled clams, which are rare near Jongno. Basic side dishes and soup can be brought directly from the self-service bar, and it is a direct ordering method. There doesn't seem to be parking, so it's better to use public transportation. Please note that the store is located on the 2nd floor. Our group ordered a large bowl of steamed clams. You can eat the basic side dishes and steamed clams after about 15 minutes using a timer, and apply the clams yourself with tongs and scissors. (There is no cutting service) There are clams and abalone on top, lily(?), red scallops, regular clams, mugwort greens, etc., and oden and boiled eggs are provided so that you can eat them later. Since the snacks are good, the alcohol goes well too. Tongyeong Port seems to have a time limit when there are a lot of people, so there is a notice posted saying that the port can be used for 2 hours and 30 minutes, so please note this if you are planning to stay for a long time. However, usually 2 hours and 30 minutes seems to be enough time. The taste was fresh and good, and after you finished eating, you could add kalguksu or sujebi, but it was money, but I didn't order it because I was full. We ordered fried shrimp while the steamed clams were cooking, and it was reasonably priced and delicious. I recommend it if you want to eat steamed or grilled clams in Jongno.

I used to often go to the Kimchi Nabe Donkatsu restaurant in Pildong. However, at some point, I lost my original intention and the food became salty and tasteless, so I stopped visiting the restaurant for a while... . As I was passing by, I happened to see that it was open.
(Dozens of days later)
As I was walking alone to eat Baekam King Sundae for lunch, a woman who appeared to be a part-time worker handed out flyers, so I accepted them and became concerned. “I lost my original intention here….” Just when I was thinking about eating pork cutlet for a while, I got the chance and headed to the restaurant.
I asked the landlady, “I came alone. Where should I sit?” asked. They said they would quickly clear the table of two people who had just left, so I stood and waited for a while and ordered a kimchi nabe.
As I sit down, food comes out from the table on the left. I was thinking it was my turn next, but then Katsudon came out. The server suddenly brought it to me. I said no. The food is then moved to the next table. Even the people next to me said no. The staff member started to panic while holding the food. I thought there must have been a mistake in ordering and asked for katsudon. The food was placed on the table, and as I was appreciating it for a moment, a man sat down at the table on my right. It looked like he had gone to the bathroom. The server confirmed the order and the katsudon went back to the customer on the right.
After waiting for a while, kimchi nabe pork cutlet came out. The size of the pork cutlet was small, but it was quite thick. I ate a bowl of rice, ate pork cutlet, and drank a spoonful of soup.

I made it. It was sour. I felt like I couldn't manage kimchi. Even if I come back, I plan to skip the kimchi nabe.

reviews.text:
The name is Busan Red French Fish Cake, but first I have to talk about Nurungji. Personally, there are times when I think of Sungnyung (especially in winter!). I often think of Korean soul food or Korean breast milk as Sungneung or Nureungji. So sometimes, when I crave the Nurungji from a Korean restaurant, I buy Nurungji at the supermarket or I buy the cup Nurungji that they sell these days and make it, but I'm always disappointed because it doesn't taste like this. However, this place is made by a Nureungji craftsman with 25 years of experience. It has already become famous after being introduced on Master of Life, so there is a backlog of orders for delivery from all over the country (sometimes it is open even at night to meet the volume of orders.) First of all, a plate of nurungji, which is spread thinly on a self-developed cauldron cast iron plate and sold for 6,000 won, is really delicious. As soon as it tastes good, I can feel the pride of Koreans who think that they can sell this nurungji like French baguettes. Moreover, the delicious nurungji is soft, crispy, savory, and really the best. And the fried Nurungji sold in a cup for 5,000 won has a completely different texture and taste than a plate of Nurungji. It tastes like a very luxurious dessert that is crispy but not hard. Sugar-free is also available depending on your preference. (I call it Zero Nurungji fried food as I like.) This was a review of the incomparable artisan Nurungji.
Still, the sign is Busan fish cake, so I can’t help but talk about oden. First of all, there are two types: regular oden and red oden. If you like fish cakes, try the soup. Haha, you'll know right away that it's not a joke. The soup is just steamy, hot, and seasoned. But the regular odeng soup tastes like the deep oden soup that my mom used to make with care. And the red odeng soup is so delicious that even if it were just sold as crab soup, it would be worth it.
And my owner's mother is someone I really like and respect. I can't write here why I think that way or what we talked about, but if you stop by this place by chance like I did and talk about various things, you will agree with my thoughts. And you will love this place.
I am one of the people who cherish and enjoy visiting this place, and I hope that this place will be visited by good people and maintained as well as it is now and for a long time.

I loved the cute and warm atmosphere, as if I was at a local Japanese restaurant. Since it was a home-cooked Japanese meal in Ikseon-dong under the rafters of a hanok, the atmosphere was already acceptable, but the taste of the food exceeded my expectations, so I was really satisfied.
​The bukkake udon at Kotokoto set menu had a really chewy and springy texture, and the chicken nambang at W set menu was also delicious. It was especially nice to be able to eat as much warm corn tea, radish radish, and rice as you wanted at the self-service bar.
The staff was very friendly and the space itself was cozy, so I had a pleasant meal. The price is reasonable, so it's a place I want to go back to when I want to eat delicious Japanese food without the burden. If you are looking for a great restaurant in Ikseon-dong, I recommend Kotokoto Restaurant.

I would like to recommend this place as it is a good Japanese restaurant in Ikseon-dong for udon and tonkatsu. It was a restaurant that caught my eye as I passed by because the exterior was emotional and cute.
Bukkake udon is a style where you pour coolly ground ice and soy sauce, and the noodles were firm and chewy, so it was really delicious. The tempura that came with it was freshly fried, so it was crispy and not greasy, so it went well with the udon.
The sirloin katsu set meal was satisfying as the meat was thick and crispy fried, and it was good to eat with cabbage salad.
It came out neatly on a tray and looked good for eating alone, and the atmosphere was also good for a light meal with friends.
This is a place I want to visit again when I want to eat udon or Japanese food in Ikseon-dong. 👍

Slightly burnt scent? Scorched scent? Should I say that? I feel a similar scent.

As indicated in the instructions, I requested additional chopped onion and minced garlic, and the taste seemed a little more balanced.
And other than that, the rest of the toppings were just okay, and when I was getting tired of eating them, I ate some Takana (Japanese stir-fried pickled mustard greens), which added a little more.

After eating it all, I thought, “It’s not my taste, but there are also rich soups like this.”

Do you have similar karma? When I think about it, something like Massugu comes to mind, but it's similar but has a completely different taste.
So, if you like tonkotsu, have already tried it here and there, and now want something new and unique, I recommend it😀

reviews.author: Kim Jang-gyeom
reviews.text:
I went to Eodam Ikseon, a hanok dining restaurant in Ikseon-dong that adds aesthetics to traditional elegance.
The moment you open the door, you will be persuaded by the atmosphere. You can feel the care put into each piece of sashimi in a quiet hanok at the end of an alley in Ikseon-dong.
The owner, a former hotel chef, has naturally incorporated a modern sensibility into a traditional Korean house based on his 12 years of experience in the United States, and thanks to the warmth of the wood and neat lighting, it is far from the hustle and bustle. The tables are spaced well apart, making it ideal for dates or quiet gatherings.
The deep flavor of aged sashimi is basic, and the flow that continues from the saltiness of steamed clams to the savory taste of grilled abalone in butter is impressive. In particular, the aged yellowtail sashimi, which is in season now, has a chewy texture and subtle sweetness that reminds me of sake. On this day, I served Yangha Daegok Celadon and it went surprisingly well with the light sashimi.

reviews.author: NU1T
reviews.text:
It tastes like Nissin chicken ramen with yuzu sauce. Soup is very clean. The yuzu sauce adds a refreshing touch. The noodles are Hosomen, the thickness of somen that I like.
The chashu is served with thick neck meat(?) lightly twisted with a torch, and it has a nice texture. The unfortunate thing is that even if you smoke it with a torch, the scent disappears once it goes into the soup. I wonder if it would be better to fry it in a frying pan like pork belly.

The addition of arugula is a good idea. Since arugula goes well with it, I wanted to try bitter chicory as well.
Menma's seasoning is milder than that of tonkotsu ramen, but I think it's because the soup is so clean that it goes well with it.

It's expensive for ramen, but you get unlimited noodles and soup for free.
As the name suggests, fried meat dumplings are similar to fried dumplings from a Chinese restaurant. it's good. Chicken Karaage is also close to fried chicken. I liked the fried meat dumplings enough to order more, but the karaage was a bit bland.

Both Soyou and Shio are cleanly delicious, but I personally think Shio goes better with yuzu sauce.
It has a different taste from tonkotsu ramen, so when you eat each one, they complement each other. Tonkotsu ➔ Yuzu ➔ Tonkotsu… After eating it for two weeks in a row, I started thinking about tonkotsu again...

It's nice that you can add toppings when ordering at the kiosk. After ordering and paying at the kiosk, give the order form to the staff, then assign a seat and take a seat.
The interior is unique in that it consists mostly of counters. There is a separate table.

The interior is surprisingly spacious and turns quickly, so there is no need to run open. If you do an open run, you should rather be assigned a corner seat.

The staff are friendly.

♤ Yuzu Tsukemen (14,000₩)
+ Kim (500₩)

I visited Yuzu Ramen, a yuzu ramen restaurant. In the case of this store, it is a joint store with 'Doma', a beef specialty store, and you can also eat grilled meat in the evening.

I ordered Tsukemen because it was available. In the case of Tsukejiru, similar to ramen, yuzu is added, so it is sour and light. The noodles are thin and well-cooked for tsukemen, and the toppings include chashu, arugula, eggs, seaweed flakes, and menma.

What I liked was that both the noodles and tsukejiru were served cold, which suited my taste for cold noodle dishes. The downside is that because it is not a tsukemen specialty restaurant, the soup stock was not available, and the noodles and menma were overcooked, so the texture was disappointing.

These days, there are so many people in Anguk that many restaurants require waiting, but the store here is quite spacious, so you can eat leisurely on weekdays.

It's so soft and tender that it can't be compared to the thick tonkatsu from famous restaurants, but the meat is so delicious that, unlike other restaurants where you only eat a lot of rice, you'll really melt into the natural meat taste of the tonkatsu.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in dumplings
Located a 6-minute walk from Exit 5 of Anguk Station.
Joraengi rice cake dumpling soup costs 19,000 won.

Light taste~
While contemplating between dumpling soup and rice cake dumpling soup, I was curious about the most expensive one, so I gave it a try~
It is said that dumpling soup contains 6 dumplings, and joraengi rice cake dumpling soup contains 4 dumplings.
I thought the dumplings would be much more expensive, but I was surprised.
And the taste of the joraengi rice cake was unexpected.
It doesn't have any special taste, it just tastes like rice cake.
It is a style that has a slightly sticky texture like glutinous rice.
The dumplings are light with a strong tofu flavor.
They serve vinegared soy sauce together, and it tastes even better when eaten together.
Personally, I vote for dumplings over joraengi rice cakes~
The soup is light, but if you add a little vinegar soy sauce, it tastes a little richer.
There was meat on top as a garnish, but the amount was not small.
Side dishes include kimchi, radish radish kimchi, and dongchimi.
It was disappointing that all three left a strange taste to my taste buds.
Is this North Korean style kimchi?

Store & Tips & Review
The store is not small and there are quite a few tables.
There is also a table for two, so it's okay to eat alone.
I visited at 5:30 pm on a weekday and the store was relaxed.
Order at the table and pay at the counter when you leave.
Waiting is a method of waiting in line at the entrance.
Dumpling soup, rice cake soup, and hot pot are served as main dishes, and there are also a few side dishes.
This is the main branch and there is a direct branch in Yeonhui-dong.

reviews.author: manbong park
reviews.text: There was no Chinese restaurant, but it’s nice to have one. I enjoyed the Jjambbong. They give me free air.

reviews.author: Lena
reviews.text: I ordered from Auto Gimbap downstairs and ate on the second floor. The crispy fried chicken and kimbap were both delicious, and although a bit expensive, the German beer was also good. The owner is kind and I want to come back to eat pho next time.

reviews.author: MAKINSTA
reviews.text:
Something went wrong...
As soon as I came in, I felt like I had made a mistake...
The lady must have been accumulating a lot, her voice full of anger...

The charm of old antiques, art shops, and traditional teahouses has disappeared. It is a tourist attraction in Seoul, and Insa-dong is a town built on commerce, so I don't like eating or buying things in Idongne...
To appease my hungry stomach a little, I went to a familiar pho restaurant, but alas.
It was Insadong...

Wealthy business owners full of their own sensibilities in priceless rip-offs... A center of strange left-wing sensibilities that have no taste but want to be seen for what they have...

Rice noodles here...
A fairly clean soup and pickled onions served as a side dish.
I asked where I saw it and it was a franchise...
But why is the price like this?
Ah... emotion... Insadong...

When I came out, it seemed like the owner of the building was running the business... so I could buy bread from the bakery on the 1st floor and buy beer from the pho restaurant on the 2nd floor. This is European again... Austrian...

A decent franchise pho restaurant.

reviews.author: Ahyung Chung
reviews.text: I went there because I heard it was a good restaurant in Insadong... but I wasn't hooked. A real Insadong restaurant! The owner is very friendly, and most of all, the food is really delicious. I ordered it on the owner's recommendation, and it was a godsend haha. If it were me, I would have had rice noodles and Vietnamese spring rolls like always. It's definitely worth giving 5 stars. I highly recommend it, everyone!!!

reviews.author: Taco Kimchi
reviews.text:
From the moment I entered the entrance, there was a pleasant smell.
I couldn't find any kindness in the lady who served me. The taste is just so-so

reviews.author: Kevin Ko
reviews.text:
A restaurant with delicious rice noodles and fried rice
They give a lot of food too.
If three people go, we get two bowls of rice noodles.
Ask them to divide it into three bowls.
I recommend ordering one more fried rice.
There is no thick meat in the rice noodles.
Add finely shredded meat.
Fried rice is also something everyone will like.
